units.text: Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java reads and writes Excel workbooks in the .xlsx format. It loads existing files and saves modified ones, supporting strict mode and repair options for damaged packages. It inspects and modifies cell contents, styles, and worksheet properties such as row height and column width. It creates and applies validation rules and conditional formatting to cells.

It reads, writes, and edits Excel workbooks through the Workbook class, which owns a WorksheetCollection of Worksheet objects, supports adding, removing, and renaming sheets, and exposes a Cells collection for reading and writing string, numeric, boolean, date/time, and formula values.

It sets font weight, border lines, fill color, cell alignment, numeric display patterns, and cell lock status through the Style object obtained from a Cell, and applies custom patterns like thousands separators with decimal places.

It enforces data validation and conditional formatting on worksheet ranges using Validation and FormatCondition objects, supporting validation types like whole number and operators such as between, and applying formatting like bold font to cells meeting specified criteria.

It creates 18 of the 25 ChartType values programmatically via ChartCollection.add() and preserves the remaining 7 ChartEx types verbatim when loading workbooks, and adds, retrieves, and removes drawing objects across 38 AutoShapeType geometries via ShapeCollection.

It configures print layout and page setup via PageSetup, freezes rows and/or columns by coordinate or cell name, and controls workbook and worksheet protection with separate passwords for structure, windows, and revisions.

It repairs malformed workbooks by setting LoadOptions to non-strict mode and enabling package and XML repair, then exposes load diagnostics through Workbook.getLoadDiagnostics() to report issues encountered during loading.

The first example creates a new workbook, names the first worksheet Report, writes a text value and a number into cells A1 and B1, applies bold formatting and a custom number format to the number, adjusts row height and column width, and saves the result as report.xlsx.

The second example loads a potentially corrupted workbook with repair options enabled, prints any repair issues found, updates the document author property, and saves the repaired workbook as output.xlsx.

Aspose.Cells FOSS for Java reads and writes Excel workbooks in the .xlsx format, supporting workbook creation, data manipulation, and formula handling for the Java 17 runtime.

Saving is currently limited to .xlsx, and ChartEx types (Waterfall, Treemap, Sunburst, Histogram, Box and Whisker, Funnel, and Map) cannot be created programmatically; charts of these types loaded from an existing workbook are preserved verbatim across load and save.
Formulas are stored and round-tripped, but the library is not a full spreadsheet calculation engine.

A handful of public XML-mapper classes are unimplemented skeleton code carried over from an early scaffold, and some APIs exist mainly to preserve OOXML metadata and package fidelity rather than to provide full Excel feature parity.

The project requires JDK 17 and Maven as the build tool. The test suite is located under src/test/java/org.aspose.cells_foss/ and contains scenario-driven integration tests for workbook behavior and XLSX round-tripping, as well as fast, focused unit tests for individual API classes without XLSX I/O.
It adds additional spreadsheet save formats beyond .xlsx, a full formula calculation engine, ChartEx chart type creation, and dedicated enterprise support.
